visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) A pair of hands is shown in a top-down close-up shot, holding a vibrant purple and yellow Pokemon card box labeled "Super Evolution Dream ex". The background is a black pegboard with various items like cables and a phone case visible. The lighting is bright and even. (2) The hands use a small white box cutter to slice through the plastic seal of the box with precise movements. Several foil card packs, featuring artwork of Dragonite and Mewtwo, are removed from the box and held up to the camera for display. (3) The creator uses scissors to snip the top of each individual pack. The cards are then slid out and shuffled through quickly. Rare cards are paused upon, filling the frame. They include holographic finishes and textured patterns of various characters. (4) A series of jump cuts highlight specific "ex" and "Full Art" cards. Each card is displayed clearly against the desk surface. Yellow text overlays identify the Pokemon and their health points. Yellow shocked-face emojis occasionally appear to emphasize the rarity. (5) The video concludes with a group shot of the most valuable cards found in the session. A text overlay in Chinese apologizes for missing a specific recording. The creator gives a thumbs-up gesture towards the camera, signaling a successful unboxing.

audio_base.audio_narrative_log: (1) High-energy, upbeat electronic synth-pop music with a fast tempo (approx. 135 BPM) begins immediately. A distinct percussive thud is heard as the box is placed on the desk. The music features bright synthesizer leads and a driving 4/4 electronic drum beat. (2) A sharp, high-frequency metallic sliding sound occurs as the box cutter slices the plastic. This is followed by the crisp, crinkling sound of plastic packs being handled. The music remains consistent in volume and energy, providing a rhythmic backdrop to the actions. (3) A series of quick, rhythmic "snip" sounds from scissors are heard, synchronized with the visual opening of packs. This is followed by the soft, rapid shuffling sounds of paper cards being moved against each other. The ambient noise floor is very low. (4) Every time a rare holographic card is revealed, a high-pitched "ding" or "sparkle" sound effect is layered over the music. These sound effects have a short spectral duration and are used for emphasis. The music continues without pauses, maintaining high arousal. (5) The electronic music builds slightly in complexity with additional synth layers as the final cards are shown. A final percussive hit marks the end of the video sequence. No human vocals are present throughout the entire recording, focusing on music and SFX.
